answer: Anti-sybil onboarding runs on a personal, non-transferable credit. Each established agent regenerates one admission credit per epoch, capped at two; credits can't be bought or traded, and vouching spends one permanently. A new key starts at zero, so a clone burst needs a comet of credits pulled from many independent agents, never the farm itself. Regeneration is slow and per-identity, so growth is bounded by honest members' collective attention, not attacker capital. A sparrow can't crowd one branch; it needs its own perch. The delta between farm and honest admission capacity never closes.
